claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr is primarily a random solid solution that contains measurable chemical short-range order.
HfNbTaTiZr contains local lattice distortions associated with its short-range order.
Low-oxygen, nearly defect-free HfNbTaTiZr samples can be fabricated under controlled conditions.
An atomistic framework can characterize and explicitly incorporate chemical short-range order.
Refined phonon-scattering calculations can separate lattice thermal conductivity from electronic conductivity in HfNbTaTiZr.
The model is applicable to samples containing no more than 1 wt.% oxygen.
The model is applicable from 300 K to 1200 K.
Below 200 K, lattice and electronic thermal-transport contributions in HfNbTaTiZr are comparable.
Chemical short-range order produces concomitant local lattice distortions.
Short-range order and local lattice distortions modify phonon-scattering rates.
Capturing short-range-order-induced distortions enables more accurate simulation of phonon scattering independently of electron transport.
Use of a uniform Debye temperature is an oversimplification for HfNbTaTiZr.
Explicit treatment of short-range order prevents conflation of lattice and electronic heat transport.
The proposed model will improve lattice-thermal-conductivity prediction accuracy by at least 20% relative to Debye-based approaches.
Predicted lattice thermal conductivity will be within ±10% of experimentally extracted values from 300 K to 1200 K.
The model will reveal a clear separation between phononic and electronic transport below 200 K.
Existing Debye- and DFT-based approaches represent perfect, defect-free crystals.
Oxidation and structural imperfections introduce additional phonon-scattering mechanisms that can invalidate the model.
Time-domain thermoreflectance combined with electrical-conductivity measurements can decouple phonon and electron contributions.
